items.text: $T$: $C\mapsto T(C)$ a fibred category over the 2-category $\mathbf{Cat}_D$; transitivity up to isomorphism.
Natural transformations $\alpha\colon u\Rightarrow v$ give $T(u)\Rightarrow T(v)$ (a group in $C$ goes to groups in $C'$ by $u$ and by $v$, homomorphic).
T\ \text{representable by } R:\qquad \underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_D(R,C)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ T(C),\quad \psi\mapsto T(\psi)(\xi),\ \ \xi\in T(R)\ \text{universal}
Aim: an algebraic structure adapted to $D$ = a 2-representable theory = an object $R$ of $\mathbf{Cat}_D$.
For $D$ = topoi: an algebraic structure = a (classifying) topos.

Exactness property as $F\colon I\to I'$ in $\mathbf{Cat}_D$: every $\varphi\colon I\to C$ factors through $I'$; fully faithful $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_D(I',C)\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_D(I,C)$ means $I'$ is generated by $I$.
“Every monoid is a group” is an exactness property: for the nerve of the monoid, the squares with multiplication and projection are Cartesian.
T(C)\to C^I\ \text{faithful}\qquad(\text{base objects indexed by a fixed set } I)
$T$ representable by $R$: base objects $I\to R$; faithfulness means $I$ generates $R$ in $\mathbf{Cat}_D$ (every object of $R$ obtained from $I$ by limit operations).
Not covered: constructions functorial only for isomorphisms; axioms not stable under limits.
“$X$ is locally constant of type $I_n$” (locally isomorphic to $I_{n,B}$) needs $\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(I_{n,B},X)$: not expressible by limits alone.
Hence “the spectrum of a ring has exactly $n$ connected components” is not expressed (connectedness is).
